name: AI-literature-review-assistant
description: AI-powered literature synthesis that turns research PDFs into citation-grounded literature reviews with claim-level traceability, RAG-based retrieval, and a PydanticAI agent for natural-language querying.

paragraphs: An AI tool to summarize research-paper PDFs into structured, citation-grounded literature review drafts.

Live demo: ai-literature-review-assistant-2jld.onrender.com (hosted on Render's free tier — the first request after a period of inactivity may take a little while to wake up). Password: AI Literature Review Assistant. The demo is read-only (READONLYDEMO, see Deployment): you can browse the pre-loaded example papers, claims, syntheses, and generated review draft, but actions that call the OpenAI API or change stored data are disabled, so the password can be shared openly here without any cost or data risk.
Example output — a review draft generated end to end from three real papers on autonomous driving (the same example data the live demo above is seeded with):
features: Sentence-level citation traceability: every sentence in a generated review draft is linked back to
Structured, validated LLM outputs: claims, syntheses, and review drafts are all extracted via OpenAI
A real, if small, extraction pipeline: PDFs are split into pages, academic sections are detected
Retrieval-augmented selection: claims and syntheses are embedded (pgvector) as they're created, so
Agentic orchestration: a PydanticAI agent (the Ask the Assistant tab) can chain the retrieval,
